title: 2001 AMC 12 Problem 17
statement: A point \(P\) is selected at random from the interior of the pentagon with vertices \(A = (0, 2),\) \(B = (4, 0),\) \(C = (2\pi + 1, 0),\) \(D = (2\pi + 1, 4),\) and \(E = (0, 4).\) What is the probability that \(\angle APB\) is obtuse?

solutions.text:
\(\angle APB = 90^\circ\) when \(P\) is on the circle with diameter \(AB,\) centered at \((2, 1)\) with radius \(\dfrac{|AB|}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{20}}{2} = \sqrt{5}.\) The angle is obtuse when \(P\) is inside this circle.

The relevant half-disk lies wholly within the pentagon, with area \(\dfrac{1}{2}\pi(\sqrt{5})^2 = \dfrac{5\pi}{2}.\)

The pentagon is the rectangle with corners \((0,0),\) \(C,\) \(D,\) \(E\) minus triangle \(OAB,\) so its area is \[ 4(2\pi + 1) - \dfrac{1}{2}(2)(4) = 8\pi. \]

The probability is \(\dfrac{\frac{5\pi}{2}}{8\pi} = \dfrac{5}{16}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: \(\angle APB\) is obtuse exactly when \(P\) lies inside the circle having \(AB\) as diameter
That semicircle lies entirely inside the pentagon, so compare its area to the pentagon’s area
